about: Shared weekly MCQ bank. Written by tools/weekly-mcqs.mjs from the app guideline text, checked by the server, approved by merging the weekly pull request. One question per line.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man presents with a lesion confined to the distal (penile) urethra. Which histologic type is most likely for this location?
questions.explain: Distal/anterior urethral tumours are commonly squamous, as stated in the histology section.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man undergoing trans‑urethral resection of a prostatic urethral tumour is found to have invasion into the prostatic stroma. What is the correct T stage for this finding?
questions.explain: Prostatic urethral T2 denotes invasion into the prostatic stroma according to the staging description.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old patient with urethral carcinoma is found to have a single inguinal lymph node metastasis (N1). According to the 2026 pathway, what is the recommended overall treatment strategy?
questions.explain: Node‑positive disease generally requires multimodal therapy rather than surgery alone, as outlined in the 2026 staging/histology‑specific pathway.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man is diagnosed with a superficial (T1) distal urethral carcinoma without nodal involvement. Which surgical principle is appropriate for this lesion?
questions.explain: Distal superficial disease can be managed with urethra‑preserving excision ensuring negative margins, per the local/nodal treatment guidance.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man has a penile squamous cell carcinoma invading the corpus spongiosum without urethral involvement. According to the UICC/AJCC TNM classification, how is the primary tumour correctly staged?
questions.explain: T2 denotes invasion into the corpus spongiosum ± urethra, whereas T3 involves the corpus cavernosum. T1b represents subepithelial connective tissue invasion with adverse features.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man undergoes radical inguinal lymphadenectomy for penile squamous cell carcinoma. Pathology reveals 4 positive inguinal nodes with extranodal extension (ENE). What is the recommended further surgical management?
options: Observation alone since the inguinal nodes have been fully excised
Prophylactic ipsilateral pelvic lymph node dissection (PLND)
Bilateral prophylactic groin irradiation without pelvic surgery
Immediate systemic chemotherapy without further pelvic staging
questions.explain: EAU guidelines recommend prophylactic ipsilateral PLND when ≥3 inguinal nodes are positive or ENE is present. Observation is insufficient given the high-risk pelvic recurrence profile.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man presents with fixed, bulky inguinal lymphadenopathy (cN3) from penile squamous cell carcinoma and is chemotherapy-fit. Which of the following is the best-established prospective cisplatin- and taxane-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy regimen?
questions.explain: TIP is the best-established prospective cisplatin/taxane neoadjuvant regimen for cN3 disease, whereas TPF has more limited prospective evidence and substantial toxicity.

questions.stem: During multidisciplinary review of a pathology report for penile intraepithelial neoplasia (PeIN), a resident asks about routine histological grading. According to ISUP 2025 guidance cited in the EAU guidelines, what is recommended regarding PeIN?
options: PeIN must be routinely graded as low, intermediate, or high grade
PeIN should not be routinely graded
PeIN grading is mandatory only if lymphovascular invasion is present
PeIN is graded using the same criteria as verrucous carcinoma
questions.explain: ISUP 2025 specifically advises not routinely grading PeIN itself. Distractors incorrectly suggest mandatory grading schemas.

questions.stem: A pathologist evaluates an HPV-associated penile squamous cell carcinoma variant. Which of the following serves as the practical surrogate marker for HPV-related pathway biology?
questions.explain: p16 IHC is noted as the practical surrogate marker for HPV-related pathway biology in HPV-associated SCC variants. Ki-67 or E-cadherin are not cited as HPV surrogates in this context.
